page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with simultaneous multithreading on the x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. The AMD EPYC 9V45 processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance is average, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling in the middle 50%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 441.73 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 46.13 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The high memory allocation relative to compute resources makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It performs adequately for static web serving and Redis SET operations, both placing in the middle 50%. However, database operations under PassMark are weak, and LLM inference speeds are poor to weak, with the 7B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%. The qualitative cost efficiency is defined by its high memory density per vCPU, offering a balanced profile for memory-bound applications, though workloads requiring high multi-threaded throughput or local NVMe storage will face performance bottlenecks.

Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage.
